title: Taking away by hopping back on a number line
examples: How do I take away on a number line?
Which way do I hop to take away?

explain.say: Look at the number line on the board. Aoife has 12 apples. She gives 5 apples away. How many apples are left? You can jump back on the number line to find out.

draw.text: Taking away by hopping back on a number line

explain.say: First, find 12 and put your finger on it. 12 is how many you start with. Taking away means going back to smaller numbers. Which way is back on the line?
Now jump back 5 times: 11, 10, 9, 8, 7. Hold up a finger for each jump. After 5 jumps back, you land on 7. 12 take away 5 is 7.
Now try 10 take away 3. Start at 10. Jump back 3 times: 9, 8, 7. 10 take away 3 is 7. Can you make the jumps with your finger?
Big jumps can help too. Here is 20 take away 10. One big jump back of 10 lands on 10. Today, try 15 take away 5 with a grown-up.

faq.q: How do I take away on a number line?
faq.a: Find the starting number, then hop back one space for each number you take away. Where you land is the answer.

faq.q: Which way do I hop to take away?
faq.a: Backwards, towards the smaller numbers. Adding hops forward, and taking away hops back.
asks: Do I hop forward or back?

faq.q: How do I keep track of the hops?
faq.a: Hold up one finger for each hop, or say them out loud. Stop when you have done the right number of hops.
asks: How do I count my hops back?

faq.a: Take away means some things are removed, so you have fewer. Twelve sweets take away five eaten leaves seven.

faq.q: Can I use a real line on the floor?
faq.a: Yes. Draw a line with chalk outside and jump backwards along it. A grown-up can make a big floor number line with you.
asks: Tell me about the number line

facts: On a number line, adding moves forward and taking away moves back.

quiz.say: Look at the sum. Start at 10 and jump back. What is the answer?
Lukas takes away on a number line. Which way does he jump?
quiz.show: Taking away on a number line. Which way?
quiz.why: Taking away jumps back, to the smaller numbers.

wrong.0: Jumping forward to bigger numbers is for adding.
wrong.1: This number line goes from side to side.
